passages.title: Passage I (Questions 51–55)
passages.body:
Our tragedy today is a general and universal physical fear so long sustained by now that we can even bear it. There are no longer problems of the spirit. There is only the question: When will I be blown up? Because of this, the young man or woman writing today has forgotten the problems of the human heart in conflict with itself which alone can make good writing because only that is worth writing about, worth the agony and the sweat. He must learn them again. He must teach himself that the basest of all things is to be afraid; and, teaching himself that, forget it forever, leaving no room in his workshop for anything but the old verities and truths of the heart, the old universal truths lacking which any story is ephemeral and doomed—love and honour and pity and pride and compassion and sacrifice. Until he does so, he labours under a curse. He writes not of love but of lust, of defeats in which nobody loses anything of value, of victories without hope and, worst of all, without pity or compassion. His griefs grieve on no universal bones, leaving no scars. He writes not of the heart but of the glands.

Until he relearns these things, he will write as though he stood among and watched the end of man. I decline to accept the end of man. It is easy enough to say that man is immortal simply because he will endure: that when the last dingdong of doom has clanged and faded from the last worthless rock hanging tideless in the last red and dying evening, that even then there will still be one more sound: that of his puny inexhaustible voice, still talking.

I refuse to accept this. I believe man will not merely endure: he will prevail. He is immortal, not because he alone among creatures has an inexhaustible voice, but because he has a soul, a spirit capable of compassion and sacrifice.
passages.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 56–60)
passages.body:
People do not understand the nature or ramifications of most educational changes. They become involved in change voluntarily or involuntarily and in either case experience ambivalence about its meanings, form, and consequences. I have implied that there are a number of things at stake—changes in goals, skills, philosophy or beliefs, behaviour, etc. Subjectively these different aspects are experienced in a diffuse, incoherent manner. Change often is not conceived of as being multidimensional. Objectively, it is possible to clarify the meaning of an educational change by identifying and describing its separate dimensions. Ignorance of these dimensions explains a number of interesting phenomena in the field of educational changes: for example, why some people accept an innovation they do not understand; why some aspects of a change are implemented and others not; why strategies for change neglect certain essential components.

The concept of objective reality is tricky. Reality is always defined by individuals and groups. But individuals and groups interact to produce social phenomena (constitutions, laws, policies, educational change programmes), which exist outside any given individual. There is also the danger that the objective reality is only the reflection of the producers of change and thus simply a glorified version of their subjective conceptions. We can reduce this problem by following the practice of posing double questions: "What is the existing conception of reality on a given issue?" Followed quickly by "says who?"

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

She accepted the prospect of her medical treatment with __equanimity__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Equanimity = calmness of mind.
Step 1: Tranquillity, composure and placidity all mean calmness, so they are synonyms.

Answer: (b).

He had been __vehement__ in opposing the idea.
questions.explanation:

Step 2: Subdued means quiet and restrained, the opposite.
Answer: (b).

All of us are living in __turbulent__ times.

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

I shall not be going to the theatre ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: First conditional.
Step 1: A future result ('shall not be going') takes the simple present in the if-clause.
Step 2: The subject 'it' takes 'snows'. So: if it snows.
Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

______ than a hundred passengers were killed in the recent train accident.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fewer vs less.
Step 1: Passengers can be counted, so we use 'fewer', not 'less'.
Step 2: 'No fewer than a hundred' stresses that the number was as large as a hundred. 'Fewest' is a superlative and cannot be followed by 'than'.
Answer: (d).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

Each of these paintings ______ made by a famous painter.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Subject-verb agreement with 'each of'.
Step 1: The subject is 'Each', which is singular, even though 'paintings' is plural.
Step 2: A singular subject takes 'is'.
Answer: (b).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

This is an area of ______ dense population.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Adverb of degree before an adjective.
Step 1: 'Dense' is a gradable adjective, so it takes a degree word like 'extremely'.
Step 2: 'Totally dense' is unnatural; 'tangentially' (indirectly) and 'languidly' (lazily) do not fit.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Affect vs effect in the passive
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

Reading ability in young children ______ by speech disorders.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Affect vs effect, and passive voice.
Step 1: 'Affect' (verb) means to influence; 'effect' (verb) means to bring about.
Step 2: The ability is influenced by disorders, so the passive 'is affected' is needed (a finite verb is required).
Answer: (d).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

She has faced almost ______ difficulty in arranging the funds for the event.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Collocation with 'almost'.
Step 1: 'Almost' fits an absolute idea: a difficulty that could almost not be overcome.
Step 2: Insurmountable means impossible to overcome, so 'almost insurmountable difficulty' is the natural phrase.
Answer: (b).

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

Our school building is ______ dilapidated.

Concept: Adverb collocation.
Step 1: Dilapidation (falling into ruin) is something one can see.
Step 2: 'Visibly dilapidated' means clearly run-down. 'Deeply' goes with feelings (deeply hurt), not with buildings.
Answer: (a).

Ranikhet is a place of remarkably ______ beauty.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: directive principles of state policy which though not justiciable are
Q: fundamental to the governance of the country and it is the duty
R: the Constitution lays down certain
S: of the state to apply these principles in making laws
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject and verb first.
Step 1: R 'The Constitution lays down certain' needs an object: P 'directive principles of state policy which though not justiciable are'.
Step 2: P ends with 'are', completed by Q 'fundamental to the governance of the country and it is the duty'.
Step 3: Q ends with 'the duty', completed by S 'of the state to apply these principles in making laws'. Order: RPQS.
Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: are evolving rapidly
Q: the geo-political and geo-economic landscape
R: where aspects related to application of military force
S: in a multipolar world is dynamic
questions.explanation:
Concept: Keep each subject next to its verb.
Step 1: Q 'The geo-political and geo-economic landscape' + S 'in a multipolar world is dynamic' forms the main clause.
Step 2: R 'where aspects related to application of military force' needs its verb P 'are evolving rapidly'.
Step 3: Order: QSRP.
Answer: (b).

P: international security, taking into account its national security interests and priorities
Q: India has participated actively in multilateral forums
R: relating to disarmament, non-proliferation and
S: in the international security arena
questions.explanation:
Concept: Subject first, then what the forums relate to.
Step 1: Q 'India has participated actively in multilateral forums' is the main clause.
Step 2: R 'relating to disarmament, non-proliferation and' is completed by P 'international security, taking into account its national security interests and priorities'.
Step 3: S 'in the international security arena' closes the sentence. Order: QRPS.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The Attorney-General of India is appointed by the President of India.
S6: He shall receive such remuneration as the President may determine.

P: In the performance of his duties, the Attorney-General shall have the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.
Q: The Attorney-General shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
R: Any person qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court can be appointed for the post.
S: The duty of the Attorney-General is to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred to him or assigned to him by the President, and to discharge the functions conferred on him by or under the Constitution or any other law for the time being in force.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Appointment, qualification, duties, rights, tenure, pay.
Step 1: After S1 (appointment), R gives who can be appointed.
Step 2: S states his duty; P adds his right of audience while performing those duties.
Step 3: Q gives his tenure, which leads to S6 on his remuneration. Order: RSPQ.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: COVID-19 was a health catastrophe that caused great distress.
S6: It triggered the movement of more than 7 million people through lockdown and post-lockdown periods.

P: India also undertook the Vande Bharat Mission.
Q: Made-in-India vaccines were sent to more than 90 countries on a commercial and grant basis.
R: India justified its credentials as a global HADR player deploying Rapid Response Teams to Maldives, Kuwait and Mauritius launching the multiphased mission SAGAR.
S: During the pandemic, India re-established its credentials as the Pharmacy of the World by supplying medicines and equipment to over 150 countries in the face of daunting logistical challenges.
questions.explanation:
Concept: S6 begins with 'It triggered the movement of people', so the sentence before it must name the evacuation mission.
Step 1: P (Vande Bharat Mission) comes just before S6.
Step 2: S (Pharmacy of the World) opens with 'During the pandemic' and links to S1. Q (vaccines) continues the supply story, R (HADR, SAGAR) adds relief work, and 'also' in P marks the last item. Order: SQRP.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The New Development Bank (NDB) has been instituted with a vision to support and foster infrastructure and sustainable initiatives in emerging economies.
S6: India is one of the largest borrowers from the Bank in the sectors of transport, health, water and financial sectors.

P: The purpose of the Bank is to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable projects in BRICS and other emerging economies.
Q: Each member country has a shareholding of 20 per cent.
R: The founding members of the NDB—Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa—brought in capital USD 1 billion as initial contribution.
S: India and other four founding members have equal shareholding in the Bank.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Purpose first, then ownership, then capital.
Step 1: P (purpose of the Bank) follows the vision in S1.
Step 2: Q (each member has 20 per cent) and S (India and the other four have equal shares) explain the shareholding; R (initial capital) completes it before S6 on India's borrowing. Order: PQSR.
Answer: (a).

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Ayurveda literally means ‘science of life’.
S6: It is about the interrelationships between these aspects.

P: Ayurveda has evolved from the various Vedic hymns rooted in the fundamental philosophies about life, disease and health.
Q: Ayurveda takes an integrated view of the physical, mental, spiritual and social aspects of human beings.
R: The Charaka Samhita and Sushruta Samhita, which developed around 2500 BCE, are the main treatises of Ayurveda.
S: According to Ayurveda, health is considered a prerequisite for achieving the goals of life, i.e., Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use the pronoun link to S6.
Step 1: S6 speaks of 'these aspects', which are named in Q (physical, mental, spiritual and social aspects). So Q comes last.
Step 2: P (origin) follows S1, R (main texts) follows P, then S (health and the goals of life). Order: PRSQ.
Answer: (a).

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The National Education Policy, 2020 is an important policy on education.
S6: The policy was formulated through consultation process at every stage—from preformulation to formulation and implementation.

P: To fulfil its objectives, it seeks to bring access, equity, quality, affordability and accountability in education for sustainable development.
Q: It has come after 34 years, replacing the National Policy on Education, 1986.
R: The policy also lays emphasis on bringing out the unique capabilities of each student, promoting ethical values, encouraging critical thinking, fostering a culture of research and encouraging rootedness and pride in India.
S: It aims to transform India into a vibrant knowledge society and global knowledge superpower by making both school and college education more holistic and flexible.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Background, aim, means, other emphases.
Step 1: Q gives background (after 34 years).
Step 2: S states the aim; P ('To fulfil its objectives') follows the aim.
Step 3: R begins with 'also', so it adds the last point before S6. Order: QSPR.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Cotton is one of the most important cash crops in India, and it makes India an important global player in cotton production.
S6: To support the cotton industry, the Government of India regularly announces Minimum Support Price (MSP) for two basic staple groups, viz., medium staple and long staple cotton.

P: Cotton sustains the livelihood of an estimated 5·8 million cotton farmers and 40-50 million people engaged in related activities such as cotton processing and trade.
Q: India's contribution to cotton production comes from around 126 lakh hectares under cotton cultivation which is around 38 per cent of the world area.
R: The country accounts for around 25 per cent of the total global fibre production.
S: In the raw material consumption basket of the Indian textile industry, the proportion of cotton is around 60 per cent.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Follow the 'global player' idea, then move to people.
Step 1: S1 calls India a global player, so R ('The country accounts for around 25 per cent of global fibre production') follows.
Step 2: Q (area under cotton) and S (share in the textile industry) give more facts.
Step 3: P (livelihood of farmers) leads to S6 on support prices for the industry. Order: RQSP.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: One of the features of humanist culture in Italy was a slackening of the control of religion over human life.
S6: There was also a concern at this time with good manners.

P: Though they were not irreligious, Italians were strongly attracted to material wealth, power and glory.
Q: He wrote a pamphlet defending acquisition of wealth as a virtue.
R: In On Pleasure, Lorenzo Valla, another humanist, criticised the Christian injunction against pleasure.
S: Francesco Barbaro was a humanist from Venice.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pronoun and 'another'.
Step 1: P explains S1 (less religious control, more interest in wealth).
Step 2: S introduces Barbaro; Q's 'He' refers to him.
Step 3: R speaks of 'another humanist', so it follows Barbaro. Order: PSQR.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Rural Postal Life Insurance was started in 1995.
S6: Therefore, various schemes of PLI and RPLI are very popular amongst eligible clients.

P: It also aims to spread insurance awareness among the rural population.
Q: However, PLI and RPLI continue to offer life insurance cover at lower premium rate and higher bonus.
R: The prime objective of the scheme is to provide insurance cover to the rural public in general and to benefit weaker sections and women workers of rural areas in particular.
S: With liberalisation of the insurance sector, Postal Life Insurance and Rural Postal Life Insurance are operating in a very competitive market.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Objective, added aim, challenge, answer.
Step 1: R gives the prime objective; P ('also aims') adds a second aim.
Step 2: S describes competition; Q ('However') answers it, which leads to S6 ('Therefore ... popular'). Order: RPSQ.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Digital Locker is a key initiative under Digital India, aimed at transforming India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
S6: These legacy documents can be electronically signed using the eSign facility.

P: Targeted at the idea of paperless governance, Digital Locker is a platform for issuance and verification of documents and certificates in a digital way.
Q: Organisations that are registered with Digital Locker can push electronic copies of documents and certificates directly into citizens’ lockers.
R: Citizens can also upload scanned copies of their legacy documents in their accounts.
S: Indian residents, who sign up for a DigiLocker account, get a dedicated cloud storage space.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Definition, users, ways to add documents.
Step 1: P defines the platform; S says who gets storage.
Step 2: Q (organisations push documents) and R (citizens 'also' upload legacy documents).
Step 3: S6 mentions 'these legacy documents', so R must come just before it. Order: PSQR.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Nano Mission Programme was initiated in 2007.
S6: The efforts of this mission are evident through India’s global ranking based on the publications in SCI journals.

P: The Nano Mission is likely to pave the path for India’s domination in cutting-edge science.
Q: Its goal is to foster, promote and develop all aspects of nanoscience and nanotechnology.
R: This is an umbrella programme which promotes basic research and focuses on nanotechnology adaptation and transfer to industry for use by masses.
S: The support under this extends to create skilled human resources, projects related to nanoscience and nanotechnology and building infrastructure of nano S&T labs at several institutes spread across the country.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pronoun reference.
Step 1: Q begins with 'Its goal', and 'Its' refers to the programme in S1, so Q comes first.
Step 2: R describes the umbrella programme and P states what it may achieve.
Step 3: S (support for people, projects and labs) leads to S6 on the results of these efforts. Order: QRPS.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

She sings much __better__ than I do.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A word that describes a verb is an adverb.
Step 1: 'Better' tells how she sings (comparative of 'well').
Step 2: So it is an adverb here.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

The story was in all the __dailies__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Plural naming word = noun.
Step 1: 'Dailies' means daily newspapers. It is preceded by 'the' and is plural.
Step 2: So it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

__Smoking__ is injurious to health.
questions.explanation:
Concept: An -ing word used as a noun is a gerund.
Step 1: 'Smoking' is the subject of the verb 'is'.
Step 2: Working as a noun, it is a gerund (a participle works as an adjective).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

What made you choose the __one__ rather than the other?
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'One' standing in for a noun is a pronoun.
Step 1: 'The one' replaces the name of a thing already in mind, just as 'the other' does.
Step 2: So 'one' is a pronoun here, not a number.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

There is still __some__ water in the bottle.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Words that come before a noun to show quantity are determiners.
Step 1: 'Some' comes before the noun 'water' and tells how much.
Step 2: So it is a determiner.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

__Hurray!__ We have won the match.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A word that expresses sudden feeling is an interjection.
Step 1: 'Hurray!' expresses joy and is followed by an exclamation mark.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

__Having__ finished her work, Sharmila left home at 8:00 PM.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Participle phrase.
Step 1: 'Having finished her work' is a perfect participle phrase that describes Sharmila.
Step 2: 'Having' begins that participle, so the expected answer is participle.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

My teacher always moves __around__ in her class while teaching.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A word that tells where an action happens and has no object is an adverb.
Step 1: 'Around' tells where she moves and is not followed by an object of its own ('in her class' is a separate phrase).
Step 2: So it is an adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

The __cantankerous__ men of the town roar around the marketplace.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A describing word before a noun is an adjective.
Step 1: 'Cantankerous' (bad-tempered) describes 'men'.
Step 2: So it is an adjective.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the word class (part of speech) of the underlined word.

India is revered as the __fountainhead__ of democracy in the world today.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Naming word = noun.
Step 1: 'Fountainhead' (source) follows 'the' and is followed by 'of democracy'.
Step 2: So it is a noun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The tragedy of our times is
questions.opt_a: we are unable to bear pain
questions.opt_b: we have forgotten the problems of the human heart
questions.opt_c: we have learnt to bear general and universal physical fear
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the line that defines 'our tragedy'.
Step 1: The passage says: 'Our tragedy today is a general and universal physical fear so long sustained by now that we can even bear it.'
Step 2: Option (b) is a result of this fear, not the tragedy itself.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What must writers learn again?
questions.opt_b: The problems of a heart in conflict with itself
questions.explanation:
Concept: Pronoun reference.
Step 1: 'He must learn them again' follows 'the problems of the human heart in conflict with itself'.
Step 2: 'Them' refers to those problems.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.theme: What belongs in a writer's workshop
questions.question: A writer's workshop should be filled with
questions.explanation:
Concept: Factual detail.
Step 1: The writer must leave 'no room in his workshop for anything but the old verities and truths of the heart, the old universal truths'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the author, the end of man is untenable because
questions.opt_d: of his spirit, born of his soul
questions.explanation:
Concept: Read the author's own reason, not the view he rejects.
Step 1: The author refuses the idea that man is immortal only because he endures or has an inexhaustible voice.
Step 2: He says man is immortal 'because he has a soul, a spirit capable of compassion and sacrifice'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The word ‘puny’ means
questions.explanation:
Concept: Vocabulary in context.
Step 1: 'His puny inexhaustible voice' contrasts a small, weak voice with its endless nature.
Step 2: Puny means small and weak, i.e. tiny.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: People do not understand the nature or ramifications of educational change because
questions.opt_a: they do not understand the multidimensional character of change
questions.opt_b: they see the certainty in the change
questions.opt_c: they are ambiguous in their decision
questions.opt_d: it takes time and hard work
questions.explanation:
Concept: Main idea.
Step 1: The passage says change is experienced 'in a diffuse, incoherent manner' and 'often is not conceived of as being multidimensional'.
Step 2: So people miss its many dimensions.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.theme: When innovation is accepted with understanding
questions.question: People would accept an innovation with understanding, if
questions.opt_a: they find meaning of the innovation in their use
questions.opt_b: there is clarity regarding its aspects
questions.opt_c: they themselves learn to innovate in their contexts
questions.opt_d: they work with their immediate and distant colleagues
questions.explanation:
Concept: Reverse the stated cause.
Step 1: 'Ignorance of these dimensions explains ... why some people accept an innovation they do not understand.'
Step 2: So clarity about its dimensions (aspects) leads to acceptance with understanding.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What is the caution the author sounds with regard to ‘objective reality’?
questions.opt_a: Objective reality is a collective reality which may have many problems
questions.opt_b: Objective reality may be influenced by subjective thinking and considerations
questions.opt_c: Objective reality is the collective influence of all people
questions.opt_d: Objective considerations are part of the subjective reality and thus they are interrelated
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the warning ('danger').
Step 1: 'There is also the danger that the objective reality is only the reflection of the producers of change and thus simply a glorified version of their subjective conceptions.'
Step 2: So objective reality may be shaped by subjective thinking.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which two words in the passage mean the opposite of the word ‘whole’?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Opposite of whole = parts.
Step 1: 'Components' and 'dimensions' both refer to separate parts of something.
Step 2: The other pairs do not mean parts.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following sums up the idea of the author?
questions.opt_a: Change is subjective and warrants objectivity from conceptualisation to implementation
questions.opt_b: Subjectivity cannot be ruled out by describing the main dimensions of change
questions.opt_c: It is difficult to conceptualise the change which satisfies all sections with understanding
questions.opt_d: Change has to be conceptualised collectively in its many dimensions, and dealt with objectively
questions.explanation:
Concept: Main idea.
Step 1: The author wants change to be understood through its separate dimensions and checked objectively by asking 'says who?'.
Step 2: Option (d) combines both ideas.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

I don't like working ______ night.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Prepositions of time.
Step 1: We say 'at night' (but 'in the morning').
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

I'll see you ______ the morning.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Prepositions of time.
Step 1: Parts of the day take 'in': in the morning, in the evening.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

There is a mark ______ the wall.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Contact with a surface.
Step 1: A mark touching the surface of the wall is 'on' it.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

Shalini usually goes to work ______ bus.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Means of transport.
Step 1: Without an article we say 'by bus', 'by train', 'by car'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

She has always been very polite ______ me.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Adjective + preposition.
Step 1: We are polite 'to' a person.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

I'm fed up ______ you.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fixed phrase.
Step 1: 'Fed up with' means annoyed or bored with.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

We had a discussion ______ the project.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Noun + preposition.
Step 1: A discussion is 'about' a topic (with is for the person you talk to).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

She is capable ______ winning the race.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Adjective + preposition.
Step 1: 'Capable of' + -ing form.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

His first novel has been translated ______ many languages.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Verb + preposition.
Step 1: Something is translated 'into' another language.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

We met a very nice family ______ our holiday.
questions.explanation:
Concept: During vs while.
Step 1: 'During' is a preposition and is followed by a noun ('our holiday').
Step 2: 'While' is a conjunction and needs a clause ('while we were on holiday').
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__During recession__ (a) __many companies were compelled__ (b) __to decrease their workforce.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Article with a countable noun.
Step 1: 'Recession' here means a particular period of economic decline and is countable, so it needs an article: 'During a recession' (or 'During the recession').
Step 2: Parts (b) and (c) are correct.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The politicians__ (a) __parted ways__ (b) __due towards ideological differences.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fixed phrase 'due to'.
Step 1: The correct phrase is 'due to ideological differences'. 'Due towards' is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The murder was__ (a) __too abominable__ (b) __to described.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Too ... to' + base verb.
Step 1: After 'to' we use the base form, and here the sense is passive: 'too abominable to be described'.
Step 2: 'To described' is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Each new word__ (a) __in this book__ (b) __have a different meaning.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Each' takes a singular verb.
Step 1: The subject is 'Each new word', which is singular.
Step 2: So 'has a different meaning', not 'have'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The news regarding__ (a) __the earthquake survivors__ (b) __are very disturbing.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'News' is uncountable and singular.
Step 1: The subject is 'The news', not 'survivors'.
Step 2: So 'is very disturbing'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__These equipments__ (a) __must have__ (b) __cost a fortune.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Uncountable noun.
Step 1: 'Equipment' is uncountable and has no plural.
Step 2: Correct: 'This equipment must have cost a fortune' (or 'These pieces of equipment').
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Prateek doesn't__ (a) __look well today,__ (b) __doesn't he?__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Question tags.
Step 1: A negative statement takes a positive tag.
Step 2: 'Prateek doesn't look well today, does he?'
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__It was one of__ (a) __most eloquent speeches__ (b) __delivered by Swami Vivekananda.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Superlative takes 'the'.
Step 1: The correct form is 'one of the most eloquent speeches'.
Step 2: The missing 'the' belongs to the superlative phrase in part (b).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Past continuous for an ongoing state
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__He suffered__ (a) __from fever when he was interviewed__ (b) __for the job.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Past continuous for a background state.
Step 1: The fever was going on at the time of the interview.
Step 2: So 'He was suffering from fever when he was interviewed'. The error is in part (a).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__She forced__ (a) __herself__ (b) __to eat.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Reflexive pronoun.
Step 1: 'She forced herself to eat' is correct: the subject and object are the same person, so 'herself' is right.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Winning the World Cup was the most __exhilarating__ moment for the Indian cricket team.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Exhilarating = very exciting and joyful.
Step 1: The closest word is 'thrilling'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Justice prevailed and the murderer was __decapitated__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Decapitate = cut off the head.
Step 1: So 'beheaded'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The hotel room had __dingy__ walls.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Dingy = gloomy and drab, dirty-looking.
Step 1: 'Dark and dirty' gives the full meaning. Hazy and cloudy describe air or sky.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Keshav planned the event with __fastidious__ care.
questions.explanation:

Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:

Her left leg was paralysed due to a __debilitating__ disease.

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Civics classes focus on citizenship and governance.
S2: The subject develops concepts that enable the reader to apply knowledge about government and the state to the idea of participative citizenship.
The second sentence
questions.explanation:
Concept: Expand = add more detail on the same idea.
Step 1: S2 explains in more detail what civics does with citizenship and governance.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: China has made rapid economic strides but at the cost of democracy.
S2: India has followed a path towards rapid economic growth, but by abiding by the norms of a democratic polity.
The second sentence
questions.opt_b: explains what is stated in the first
questions.opt_c: offers a contrast to the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Contrast = shows a different case side by side.
Step 1: S2 does not deny S1. It shows India growing with democracy, against China growing at its cost.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The concept of right or wrong needs to be determined on the basis of principles.
S2: When it comes to matters related to the field of human rights, positions should be based solely on principles.
The second sentence
questions.opt_b: develops an axiom based on the first
questions.opt_d: delegitimises the premise of the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: General rule to a specific rule.
Step 1: S1 is a general principle. S2 applies it to one field (human rights) as a rule of its own.
Step 2: S2 does not prove S1, so it does not 'establish' it. It develops a working rule (axiom) from it.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The concept of Ahimsa was adopted by Gandhiji after he was introduced to it by Tolstoy. The latter first read about it in German translation of Thirukkural, the great moral treatise in Tamil.
S2: Much in the same way that Gandhi was influenced by Tolstoy, in the United States of America, Martin Luther King Jr. shaped his Civil Rights Movement based on Gandhian principles.
The second sentence
questions.opt_b: defends the premise of the first
questions.opt_c: provides an analogy for the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Analogy = a similar case.
Step 1: 'Much in the same way' signals a parallel: King learnt from Gandhi as Gandhi learnt from Tolstoy.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The best ever cricket captain India has ever had is XYZ.
S2: As captain, XYZ has won considerably more matches for India than any other captain.
The second sentence
questions.opt_b: is the premise for the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Premise = the reason on which a claim rests.
Step 1: S2 gives the reason (most wins) for the claim in S1 (best captain).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.opt_b: Compliment means to go well with and complement means to praise

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Stationery’ and ‘Stationary’
questions.opt_a: Stationery means standing still and stationary means immobile
questions.opt_b: Stationery means writing and office material and stationary means in station
questions.opt_c: Stationery means writing and office material and stationary means immobile
questions.opt_d: Stationery means standing still and stationary means writing and office material

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Complaisant’ and ‘Complacent’
questions.opt_a: Complaisant means overconfident and complacent means eager to please
questions.opt_b: Complaisant means confident and complacent means overconfident
questions.opt_c: Complaisant means eager to please and complacent means to manifest universally
questions.opt_d: Complaisant means eager to please and complacent means overconfident
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complaisant vs complacent.
Step 1: Complaisant = willing to please others.
Step 2: Complacent = too self-satisfied, careless because overconfident.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Enquiry’ and ‘Inquiry’
questions.opt_a: Enquiry means to seek information and inquiry means to investigate
questions.opt_b: Enquiry means to investigate and inquiry means to seek information

questions.opt_d: Enquiry means act of investiture and inquiry means to investigate

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Masterful’ and ‘Masterly’
questions.opt_a: Masterful means imperious and masterly means autocratic
questions.opt_b: Masterful means skilful and masterly means imperious
questions.opt_c: Masterful means leader-like and masterly means skilful
questions.opt_d: Masterful means imperious and masterly means highly skilful
questions.explanation:
Concept: Masterful vs masterly.

Step 2: Masterly = done with great skill.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Boarder’ and ‘Border’
questions.opt_a: Boarder means a food-and-lodge resident and border means boundary
questions.opt_b: Boarder means boundary and border means a food-and-lodge resident

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Concurrent’ and ‘Consecutive’
questions.opt_a: Concurrent means occurring at the same time and consecutive means occurring one after the other
questions.opt_b: Concurrent means occurring non-simultaneously and consecutive means occurring one after the other
questions.opt_c: Concurrent means occurring at the same time and consecutive means occurring thereafter
questions.opt_d: Concurrent means occurring thereafter and consecutive means occurring at the same time
questions.explanation:
Concept: Concurrent vs consecutive.
Step 1: Concurrent = happening at the same time. Consecutive = following one after another without a break.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

‘Epitaph’ and ‘Epithet’
questions.opt_a: Epitaph means a tombstone and epithet means a phrase expressing an attribute
questions.opt_b: Epitaph means words written on a tombstone and epithet means a phrase expressing an attribute
questions.opt_c: Epitaph means unspoken words and epithet means a phrase expressing an attribute
questions.opt_d: Epitaph means words written on a tombstone and epithet means an epigram
questions.explanation:
Concept: Epitaph vs epithet.
Step 1: An epitaph is the words written on a tombstone, not the stone itself.
Step 2: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase (e.g. 'the Great').
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both words.

questions.opt_b: Discomfort means unease and discomfit means to embarrass

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Match the items in the first list with the second list and choose the correct code.

List I (Loan word)
A. Attaché

List II (Meaning)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Match the items in the first list with the second list and choose the correct code.

List I (Loan word)
A. Sui generis
B. Facta non verba
C. Mutatis mutandis
D. Non sequitur

List II (Meaning)
1. Remaining same despite changes
2. Conclusion not drawn from stated logic
3. Nothing else like it
4. Deeds not words
questions.explanation:
Concept: Latin phrases.
Step 1: Sui generis = unique, nothing else like it (3). Facta non verba = deeds not words (4).
Step 2: Mutatis mutandis = with the necessary changes made, the rest staying the same (1). Non sequitur = a conclusion that does not follow (2). Code: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

Expatriate

She was advised by her coach to ______ to form if she wanted to do well in the tournament.

Directions: Choose the phrasal verb that best fills the blank.

She said goodbye and ______ along the road.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Phrasal verb meaning.
Step 1: 'Trip off' (old-fashioned) means walk away with light, quick steps.
Step 2: 'Tripped over' means stumbled over something, which does not fit 'along the road'.
Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:

The team reported that they had ______ the contract with a fine-tooth comb before forwarding its recommendation.

The boisterous crowd ______ with its merry-making even amidst pouring rain.

Step 2: 'Played on' is used without 'with'; 'carried out' means performed a task.

The goons ______ the unsuspecting victims when the latter walked into the dark alley.

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Read both sentences. Decide whether the underlined word is used correctly in each.

S1: What is __especially__ noticeable about the pair is that they always dress impeccably.
S2: Lunch is served late in the office, __specially__ on days when there is a board meeting.
questions.opt_a: S1 is right and S2 is wrong
questions.opt_b: S1 is wrong and S2 is right
questions.opt_c: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
questions.opt_d: Both S1 and S2 are right
questions.explanation:
Concept: Especially vs specially.
Step 1: 'Especially' means particularly, above all. S1 uses it correctly.
Step 2: S2 means 'particularly on board-meeting days', so it needs 'especially'. 'Specially' means for a special purpose (specially made). S2 is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Read both sentences. Decide whether the underlined word is used correctly in each.

S1: The matter was resolved amicably __between__ the group even though there were so many of them.
S2: __Among__ them the two never have problems sharing what they have.
questions.opt_a: S1 is right and S2 is wrong
questions.opt_b: S1 is wrong and S2 is right
questions.opt_c: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
questions.opt_d: Both S1 and S2 are right
questions.explanation:
Concept: Between vs among.
Step 1: S1 speaks of many members, so 'among' is needed; 'between' is wrong.
Step 2: S2 speaks of two people, so 'between' is needed; 'among' is wrong. Both are wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Read both sentences. Decide whether the underlined word is used correctly in each.

S1: We __shall__ have to present ourselves before the Dean and explain our behaviour.
S2: They __will__ need to get their act together if they wish to win the contract.
questions.opt_a: S1 is right and S2 is wrong
questions.opt_b: S1 is wrong and S2 is right
questions.opt_c: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
questions.opt_d: Both S1 and S2 are right
questions.explanation:
Concept: Shall vs will.
Step 1: 'Shall' with 'we' for the future is correct (formal British usage).
Step 2: 'Will' with 'they' is correct. Both are right.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Read both sentences. Decide whether the underlined word is used correctly in each.

S1: I have not seen her __since__ a long time.
S2: It has been a while __since__ I saw her.
questions.opt_a: S1 is right and S2 is wrong
questions.opt_b: S1 is wrong and S2 is right
questions.opt_c: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
questions.opt_d: Both S1 and S2 are right
questions.explanation:
Concept: Since vs for.
Step 1: 'Since' goes with a point in time; a length of time takes 'for'. S1 should be 'for a long time', so it is wrong.
Step 2: S2 'since I saw her' marks a point in time, so it is right.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS I 2024 English set A (set code SRSU-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Read both sentences. Decide whether the underlined word is used correctly in each.

S1: The teacher enquired whether there is __any__ problem with the question paper.
S2: He asked her whether she had __some__ pets at home.
questions.opt_a: S1 is right and S2 is wrong
questions.opt_b: S1 is wrong and S2 is right
questions.opt_c: Both S1 and S2 are wrong
questions.opt_d: Both S1 and S2 are right
questions.explanation:
Concept: Any vs some in questions.
Step 1: In questions (including reported 'whether' questions) we normally use 'any'. S1's 'any' is correct.
Step 2: S2 should be 'whether she had any pets', so 'some' is wrong.
Answer: (a).
